evidence.text: The database analyzes 大 as a front-facing standing adult with arms hanging down. It proposes ‘adult’ as an original sense, contrasted with child, and derives ‘big’ from that contrast. It reports bronze 大 used opposite 小, citing 郘鐘「大鐘八聿(肆)」, and says early 大 and 夫 shared a graph before 夫 was differentiated by adding a short stroke, often treated by scholars as decorative. These are the database’s analyses; it does not provide a dated sequence establishing the adult-to-big semantic link.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 漢字甲骨部件分析：大

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 大 entry: Shuowen text, readings and senses
evidence.text: The entry reproduces the Shuowen explanation that 大 depicts a human and records its ancient-form relationship with 亣. It lists modern Mandarin readings dà, dài and tài and describes senses including large, older or higher-ranking person, and use as a substitute for 太/泰. The cited older texts illustrate uses, but the entry does not establish their chronological order as a semantic chain.

evidence.source: Kim, Mi Seong, Journal of Chinese Language and Literature
evidence.text: The 2020 article describes oracle-bone 大 as shaped like a frontal human figure and says 大 and 小 already had varied uses in the oracle-bone period. Its abstract does not give individual dated 大 attestations or establish the adult-to-large semantic link.

gaps: No individual oracle-bone specimen was retrieved for pixel inspection. The Commons file description identifies a Sinica source image, but its original image retrieval failed in the web tool.
The Commons glyph files are modern digital redrawings, not photographs of ancient artifacts. Captions should identify the script style and redraw status.

No exact earliest dated attestation of 大 for ‘adult’ or ‘big’ was established. CUHK cites a bronze inscription for ‘big’, but the cited vessel’s date and inscription were not independently verified here.

The adult-to-big semantic relation is CUHK’s explicit analysis; evidence for intermediate semantic stages was not collected. Other historically listed senses and readings do not establish a chronology by themselves.
The outstretched-arms account in dossier excerpts conflicts with CUHK’s arms-hanging-down description. No image pixels were inspected to settle the depiction directly.

The broad historical sequence from oracle-bone/bronze forms to seal and later scripts is represented by identified file styles, but specific stroke-by-stroke changes, scribal corruption and variant chronology remain unestablished.
No sound component or whole-graph phonetic loan is proposed for standalone 大; no source-word/object-name reconstruction is relevant to this analysis.
